names.name: the Self known by itself (svasaṃvedya ātmarūpa)

descriptions: the Primal One set forth by the Vedas, known by itself, whose form is the Self (Jñāneśvarī 1.1)
the one reality that appears as Śiva and Śakti and sports as the world (Amṛtānubhava)
the beautiful form standing on the brick, hands on hips, mother to the devotee
smaller than an atom and vast as the sky (Tukārām)
negations: not described by sat, cit or ānanda, which only exclude their opposites (Amṛtānubhava 5)
not reached by the word, which ends before the self-evident (Amṛtānubhava 6)
relation_to_self: The Self is the Lord; yet devotion continues after knowledge — God worships God.
relation_to_world: The world is the play of the one consciousness, not a second thing; seen through the saints it is the Lord's (onion and radish are Viṭṭhala).
caveat: The Vārkarīs hold the personal Viṭṭhala and the non-dual Self together; they would reject a reading that makes the form merely provisional for beginners.

descriptions: the supreme Brahman who, formless, becomes embodied through the devotee's love (Mānas 1.116)
the master in the form of all moving and unmoving beings (Mānas 4.3)
whose name is greater than both his forms (Mānas 1.18–28)
negations: without qualities, without form, unseen, unborn (Mānas 1.116)
relation_to_self: The soul is Rāma's servant; the exclusive devotee holds 'I am the servant' unwaveringly.
relation_to_world: The world is full of Sītā and Rāma and to be bowed to; seen through māyā ('I and mine') it binds, and is like a dream beside worship of Hari.
caveat: The tradition would reject any reading that makes the embodied Rāma lower than the formless; the name is held greater than both.

descriptions: love (hita) itself, appearing as the pair in eternal play
Rādhā, whose favour even Madhusūdana seeks
negations: no separation, birth-story or departure in the eternal play
relation_to_self: The soul's true identity is as a sakhī who delights in the pair's joy.
relation_to_world: The world is not the focus; the eternal Vṛndāvana is the reality contemplated.
caveat: The tradition rejects making Rādhā a power of Kṛṣṇa or reducing the pair's love to an impersonal absolute; love, not Brahman, is its first term.

names.name: Kuñjabihārī and Śyāmā, the natural pair (sahaja jorī)

descriptions: the pair eternally together in the grove, never joined and never parted
negations: not born, not separated, not newly united
relation_to_self: The devotee is a sakhī who serves and witnesses.
relation_to_world: The world's pursuits are empty; death is ever near; live as Hari keeps you.
caveat: The pair is held to be one reality in two forms; the tradition would reject an impersonal reading.

descriptions: the dark one wearing the peacock crown, her husband
relation_to_self: The soul is his bride and servant.
relation_to_world: Family honour and the world's shame are to be cast off for him.
caveat: A song-tradition without a formal theology; songs using the name ('Rām ratan') are read by some as nirguṇa, by most as devotion to Kṛṣṇa.

descriptions: the one Supreme, distinct from souls, deities and world, who alone liberates and incarnates as the five Kṛṣṇas
relation_to_self: Souls are eternally distinct from Parameśvara and are liberated by his grace.
relation_to_world: The world (prapañca) is an eternal reality of māyā, distinct from him.
caveat: The Mahānubhāvas insist on the distinctness of Parameśvara from the Vedic and Purāṇic gods and from souls; they reject the identification of all gods as forms of one truth.

descriptions: the eternal one whose form is Brahman, Nārāyaṇa, cause of all avatāras (Kīrtana-ghoṣā)
the root whose watering nourishes all the gods
relation_to_self: The soul is Kṛṣṇa's servant; the devotee seeks devotion, not liberation.
relation_to_world: Other gods and rites belong to the world; Kṛṣṇa alone is refuge.
caveat: The tradition itself refuses worship of other deities; it would reject a reconciliation that makes all deities equal objects of refuge, even while holding that worship of Kṛṣṇa satisfies all.

descriptions: Rāma, reached by the path of devotion
the formless Brahman beyond the elements, known by discrimination
negations: not the elements, not the body
relation_to_self: The Self beyond body and elements is Brahman; the accomplished abide in it.
relation_to_world: The world is to be lived in with effort and vigilance while knowing the Self.
caveat: Devotion to Rāma and Advaita discrimination are held together; neither is dropped.

descriptions: you alone, Śrī Hari, appear in endless forms (Narsinh)
Brahman is one for king and servant (Annamācārya)
relation_to_self: Varies by poet; Narsinh: until the Self is known all practice is false.
caveat: Not a tradition: a classificatory grouping; each poet's view should be read with the tradition that claims him.
